title: Triage review of c31's crawlers from noise on seeds 7 and 8: cells with their own s layer form from the random field and polarize, but they merge into one or two large crawlers that cover 2.0 and 1.7 body lengths, short of the 3-length M gate
summary: Labkit re-runs of world.py at defaults, seeds 7 and 8 (256^2, 80 frames, t=16). Both start from the thresholded random field (sheet t=0), give 6-8 round cells by t~0.6-1.4, each with a ring of s (radial s rim/core 4.2, rim/out 12, 12 of 17 individuals membrane-like on seed 7); the larger cells polarize into half-moons, crawl, and absorb the cells they touch, ending with 2 (seed 7) and 1 (seed 8) components. labkit motion: max 2.0 (seed 7) and 1.7 (seed 8) body lengths per track, in sqrt(area), which is the right unit for a half-moon that moves broadside; on seed 7 the big crawler keeps moving from t~7 to 16 but its track is cut by the merges.

observations.S: rerun/seed7/sheet.png t=0: random two-phase field over the whole box
observations.B: rerun/seed7/FACTS.md radial s rim/core 4.2, rim/out 12, 12/17 membrane-like

seeds_run.result: partial: S I B yes, motion 2.0 body lengths
partial: S I B yes, motion 1.7 body lengths

verdicts.limitation: M: on both fresh seeds no labkit track reaches 3 body lengths (2.0 and 1.7), because the crawlers merge with the cells they touch; I did not measure displacement across merges by hand, so I list M as not reached rather than contradicted. I did not read the B code against the quasi-equilibrium clause or run the source-off arm.
